Q1: Which branch should the fix be built on and merged into?
Choices:
A) PR #7044's head branch `ai/issue-6769`, where the failure happened. The implementer adds an `Integration branch: ai/issue-6769` line so the fix PR targets that branch. (RECOMMENDED)
B) The default branch (`main`): the failure is assumed to come from code already on `main`, and PR #7044 picks up the fix when it syncs.
C) The default branch first; if the failure doesn't reproduce there, `ai/issue-6769` instead.
Q2: The failing test name isn't available. How should the implementer find the failure, and what if it doesn't reproduce?
Choices:
A) Run the `orchestrate-poll` group 3 / shard 0 subset of `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py` on the target branch using the partition in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, falling back to the whole module. Then make the smallest fix for the first real failure. If every test passes, treat it as a flaky or environmental failure and close with no code change. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Do A, and also have the CI shard runner print each failing shard's first `FAIL` line or traceback, plus the reason when a shard recorded no exit code, in the job's final summary. That way later triage issues include the test name. **Note:** this edits `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, which needs an exact `files_touched` grant (automation-path guard).
C) No investigation: re-run CI on PR #7044 and close this issue if it passes.
